podcast.body: This album resulted from David Bowie convincing Iggy Pop, the Ashton brothers, and James Williamson to come to England to make a record for Columbia Records. Despite Bowie's connection and influence, the album struggled commercially, peaking at 182 on the Top 200 charts. However, it deeply inspired many artists, including a 16-year-old Johnny Lydon and Mick Jones (The Clash) who were at Iggy's first UK show, and Kurt Cobain who later called it his favorite album. "But the people who bought this record were inspired."

podcast.body: This album was created with the patronage of David Bowie, who convinced his manager to invest cash into The Stooges project. The album was intentionally designed to be extremely intense, aiming to "actually hurt people as it came out of the speakers." It features the song "Search and Destroy." "The result was an injection of cash that was enough to make an album that was designed to be so intense that it would actually hurt people as it came out of the speakers."
